It seems that in react-leaflet version 3, [the url prop for the TileLayer is immutable](https://react-leaflet.js.org/docs/v3/api-components/#tilelayer), so apparently changing the url from a react perspective won't work.

The fix was to add a new tile layer in the toggle method of the Map.tsx and then adding a new layer and then setting the url of the layer that way.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: mabruzzo
body:
This fixes some failing tests of the VL+CT integrator, that arose because of a recent change in `yt` that affected the python script for computing the L1 Error Norm. I also did some light refactoring.

When accessing field data, the script used a single string to specify the name of the field. Recent versions of `yt` now require that we fully specify the two part names of fields. For more context, I provide a concrete example below:
-  we could previously access density data by specifying  `data['density']`. 
- In reality, `yt` didn't directly track a field called `'density'`. Instead it tracked a field called `'enzoe', 'density'` (this field is specific to enzo-e, corresponds to the data stored on disk, and is in code units) and a field called `'gas', 'density'` (this is a field derived from `'enzoe', 'density'` and has cgs units). Previously, `yt` would translate `density` into one of these two choices under-the-hood
- the latest version of `yt` requires that we directly access density by specifying `data['gas','density']` or `data['enzoe','density']`. This removes some ambiguity.

This PR is meant to provide a short-term fix so that these failing tests don't interfere with the review of other PRs (like PR #199).

With that said, the script is a bit of a mess. A lot of complexity arises from the fact that it supports compute the L1 Error Norm when comparing 2 different snapshots and when comparing a snapshot with a tabulated solution (like for a shock tube). Cleaning this script up is definitely on my ToDo list (I also want to migrate the tests using this script to the pytest framework and add the ability to compute the l1 error norm for simulation that use AMR)

body: This adds reminders for teachers who have an `incomplete` application, i.e. teachers who have saved an application but have not submitted it. See [spec](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1I2WXc7REV0QdZ5EaxjHBj36CDkawmcw-xQyEvZcFHao/edit#) for the content ("First Reminder Complete Your Application" and "Second Reminder Complete Your Application" –– do a find for these in the doc, as I don't think they're linked at the top). We are sending the first reminder (`initial_reminder`) if they haven't updated their application in 7 days. We send the second reminder (`final_reminder`) if they haven't updated their application in 14 days. Mailers look like this: UPDATED final reminder: ## Links ## Testing story ## Deployment strategy ## Follow-up work ## Privacy ## Security ## Caching ## PR Checklist: - [ ] Tests provide adequate coverage - [ ] Privacy and Security impacts have been assessed - [ ] Code is well-commented - [ ] New features are translatable or updates will not break translations - [ ] Relevant documentation has been added or updated - [ ] User impact is well-understood and desirable - [ ] Pull Request is labeled appropriately - [ ] Follow-up work items (including potential tech debt) are tracked and linked

This is a revamp of the config editor pages in terms of providing table of contents navigation within the pages. To see the pages live while reviewing this PR, you will need to edit your local copy of /src/gatsby-theme-carbon/components/LeftNav/ResourceLinks.js and change the configeditor doc link to your localhost, e.g. href: 'https://localhost:8000/configeditor/index.html' and re-run 'gatsby develop'.

Also, there is one place in the main docs (/migration/migrate-file-storage/) that points to the Config Editor page.  In your local copy, you will need to edit the "Install CE" link in this file to your localhost instance if you are testing it live locally.

Remove ID tokens when the associated access and refresh tokens are cleared.

Preserve expired tokens until the associated access token is deleted to keep relationships intact and not trigger delete cascades.

author: michaelkirk
body:
Simplify, use length not cost, and prefer non-empty 

Short trips would often just not have a route name since they didn't pass the threshold of minimal cost.

Previously it was based on "cost" not length, which would mean that, e.g. driving down a long stretch of road with a left turn just before the arrival, would be named after the left turn rather than the 99% of your trip. I think length is a more intuitive naming mechanism for routes than cost.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: kellyma2
body:
Init containers must be idempotent because they may get re-run in some cases even if the pod itself is not being restarted. For example, if the underlying node garbage collects the associated docker container.

In the current incarnation of the init script we will fail if the init container is re-run resulting in a state where the init container is continually flapping.  To avoid this, we can add a initialization check file and short circuit the initialization process if it is present.
